topics.title: Validation checks
topics.summary: Choose which checks run before delivery.
topics.whenToUse: Select checks that can prove this task's result, using commands and targets configured for its repository.
topics.behavior: Workflow selects the phases. The launch's Repository project setup supplies commands and web targets; the task supplies acceptance facts; the AI setup supplies Reviewer. Saved checkboxes do not prove that checks ran or passed.
topics.defaultBehavior: New Workflows enable validation setup, build, tests and review by default. Saved selections may differ. Advisory browser QA is off by default.
topics.impact: Missing required commands can block launch. Enabled checks may skip when their prerequisites are unmet.
topics.example: Enable Build here, then configure the build command under Repository → Project setups. Check the launch preview for the actual selection.

options.setup: Prepares the workspace before validation commands run.
options.lint: Checks code style and quality using the lint command.
options.sast: Runs the project's source-code security analysis command.
options.build: Builds the project using its configured command.
options.test: Runs the test command configured for the project.
options.health: Starts the app and checks that its endpoint responds.
options.pages: Checks configured pages and their CSS assertions.
options.facts: Checks explicit proof requirements supplied with the task.
options.review: Reviews the result against the task using AI Reviewer.
options.advisory: Adds optional browser feedback; it is not a blocking gate.

topics.title: Validation setup
topics.summary: Prepares the workspace before validation commands run.
topics.whenToUse: Use for repeatable preparation needed by validation, such as seeding test data.
topics.behavior: Runs validationSetupCommand before the blocking checks. This is distinct from image preparation and the Repository prepare command. A failure prevents later blocking checks from running.
topics.defaultBehavior: Enabled in a new Workflow, but no validation setup command means there is nothing to run and this phase is skipped.
topics.impact: The Repository setup's build timeout also bounds validation setup. Keep preparation repeatable across validation attempts.
topics.example: Configure a test-data seed command as validation setup; do not put image installation or a deployment here.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Commands → Setup command (validationSetupCommand)

topics.title: Lint
topics.summary: Checks code style and quality using the lint command.
topics.whenToUse: Enable when the repository has a reliable lint command.
topics.behavior: Runs the selected project setup's lintCommand before build. A lint failure is a validation failure; later Facts/Review wait for prerequisite checks to succeed.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off in a new Workflow. Selecting Lint with a Repository setup that has no lint command blocks launch.
topics.impact: Uses the Repository setup's lint timeout. Enabling this check does not install a linter or choose its rules.
topics.example: Configure npm run lint in the Repository setup, then enable Lint in the Workflow.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Commands → Lint command (lintCommand)

topics.title: Static security analysis (SAST)
topics.summary: Runs the project's source-code security analysis command.
topics.whenToUse: Enable when the project has a configured static security-analysis tool.
topics.behavior: Runs sastCommand after lint and before build. This is separate from Workflow's built-in Security scans for repository content such as secrets, personal data and prompt injection.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off in a new Workflow. Selecting SAST with a Repository setup that has no SAST command blocks launch.
topics.impact: Uses the Repository setup's SAST timeout. This switch does not install a scanner or replace the content-scan policy.
topics.example: Configure semgrep with the project's chosen rules as the SAST command, then enable this phase.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Commands → SAST command (sastCommand)

topics.title: Build
topics.summary: Builds the project using its configured command.
topics.whenToUse: Enable for work that must compile or produce a build result.
topics.behavior: Runs buildCommand from the selected Repository project setup. Build/prerequisite results determine whether subsequent app checks, Facts and Review can run meaningfully.
topics.defaultBehavior: Enabled in a new Workflow. Selecting Build with a Repository setup that has no build command blocks launch.
topics.impact: Uses the Repository setup's build timeout and build variables. This checkbox does not infer a build command from the repository.
topics.example: Repository Example → Project setup Development → Build command: npm run build.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Commands → Build command (buildCommand)

topics.title: Tests
topics.summary: Runs the test command configured for the project.
topics.whenToUse: Enable when automated tests can verify the change.
topics.behavior: Runs the selected Repository setup's testCommand. It does not invent tests from the task description or assume every test suite is included in that command.
topics.defaultBehavior: Enabled in a new Workflow. Selecting Tests with a Repository setup that has no test command blocks launch.
topics.impact: Uses the Repository setup's test timeout and build variables. A failing suite is not the same as a test infrastructure failure.
topics.example: Choose a focused, repeatable project test command such as npm test; configure its scope in the Repository setup.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Commands → Test command (testCommand)

topics.title: App health
topics.summary: Starts the app and checks that its endpoint responds.
topics.whenToUse: Use for a web app or HTTP service that validation can start and probe.
topics.behavior: Uses startCommand, healthPath and healthTimeout from the Repository setup. Health needs a successful build result; a project marked as having no web UI skips web checks.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off in a new Workflow. Selecting Health with a Repository setup requires a start command at launch.
topics.impact: Starts a process during validation. Browser smoke pages depend on Health actually passing, not merely being enabled.
topics.example: Configure the start command and /health path in the Repository setup, then enable App health.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Start command + Validation → health path, timeout and web-UI flag

topics.title: Browser smoke pages
topics.summary: Checks configured pages and their CSS assertions.
topics.whenToUse: Use to verify that important web pages render and contain expected elements or text.
topics.behavior: Visits smokePages from the selected Repository setup and checks exists, visible, text-contains or count assertions. Pages run only after Health passes and when pages are configured.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off in a new Workflow. With no pages or non-passing Health, the phase is skipped. Selecting web validation also requires a Repository start command at launch.
topics.impact: Needs a web project and browser-capable validation infrastructure. This is a configured smoke test, not exploratory UX review.
topics.example: Add /settings with a visible h1 assertion in Repository → Project setups → Smoke pages; enable App health and Browser smoke pages.
topics.source: Repository → Project setups → Smoke pages (smokePages); App health is a prerequisite

topics.title: Required acceptance facts
topics.summary: Checks explicit proof requirements supplied with the task.
topics.whenToUse: Use when the task's structured acceptance spec contains concrete artifacts or commands that must be verified.
topics.behavior: Executes the task contract's requiredFacts after prerequisite checks. This checkbox does not generate facts from ordinary task prose. Facts awaiting a human deviation decision can keep Review from running.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off in a new Workflow. No required facts means this phase is skipped, even when enabled.
topics.impact: Keep required facts enabled when the supplied task spec relies on them. Skipping is not evidence that an acceptance requirement passed.
topics.example: Supply a structured spec requiring a particular artifact and a passing command, then enable Facts. The task, not this Workflow, owns those requirements.

topics.title: AI review
topics.summary: Reviews the result against the task using AI Reviewer.
topics.whenToUse: Use automated review alongside concrete build, test and acceptance checks.
topics.behavior: Uses the selected AI setup's Reviewer route and the task's review inputs. Review waits for prerequisite checks and required facts; failed or pending-human Facts can defer it.
topics.defaultBehavior: Enabled in a new Workflow. Disabling this phase skips automated task review; it does not change the AI setup's selected Reviewer.
topics.impact: Uses model tokens and time. AI review is not a replacement for tests, a human approval, or permission to merge.
topics.example: Choose an independent Reviewer in the AI setup, then enable AI review here. The launch selects which AI setup is used.
topics.source: AI setup → Reviewer; review requirements come from the task

topics.title: Advisory browser QA
topics.summary: Adds optional browser feedback; it is not a blocking gate.
topics.whenToUse: Use for supplementary browser observations against the task's scenario or human-review checklist.
topics.behavior: Runs only after blocking validation passes, with passing App health, a web UI, and scenario or human-review checklist input. It uses Reviewer and browser infrastructure. No checklist or unmet prerequisites means it may skip or not run.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off by default. Both advisoryBrowserQaEnabled and the advisory phase must be enabled. The desktop checkbox edits those two settings together.
topics.impact: Adds browser/model work but does not turn observations into blocking acceptance requirements. Use smoke pages or required facts for enforceable checks.
topics.example: Supply a scenario checklist, enable App health and advisory QA, and inspect the resulting observations separately from the blocking validation result.
topics.source: Repository web targets + task scenario/human-review checklist + AI setup's Reviewer

topics.title: Validation attempts
topics.whenToUse: Allow a limited number of attempts when an agent may need to correct a failed check.
topics.behavior: The initial validation counts as attempt 1. Failed validation can return findings to the agent for correction while attempts remain. Exhaustion stops the automatic correction loop and requires review; it does not authorize delivery.
topics.defaultBehavior: Default 3, supported range 1–10. One permits the initial validation without an automatic correction retry. Explicit recovery/rework paths have their own accounting rules.
topics.impact: More attempts can add validation time and agent/model use. This is not the failover switch limit or a per-command retry count.
topics.example: A limit of 2 allows the initial validation and, when safe and applicable, one correction/revalidation cycle.
